parallel.requirements: Recognized the task as three requirements: value-analysis CPA worklist, predicate analysis with path feasibility, and k-induction/BMC, with all 12 benchmark signals required.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Used one main actor despite swarm mode being enabled, explicitly choosing sequential local ownership because v1 depended on v0 and v3 depended on v1.
parallel.implementation: Implemented value_analysis.py, predicate_analysis.py, bmc.py, and k_induction.py; created requirement patches and commits for cpachecker_v0, cpachecker_v1, and cpachecker_v3.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Integrated all stages in the same workspace, committed each requirement, generated three non-empty requirement patch files, and supplied one regression test file.
parallel.verification: Ran focused v3 checks and the full run.sh suite; the final raw run reported 12/12 correct and the official evaluation passed all v0, v1, and v3 tests.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished required stage is visible at closure; the only taxonomy-relevant issue is that the parallel-mode trajectory did not actually execute a parallel child mechanism.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same three CPAchecker requirements. The second round specifically reread the v3 k-induction/BMC requirement after the first round stopped.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Used one local actor with Agent and AgentSwarm disabled. It planned and owned the stages serially, with no delegation or child handoff.
serial.implementation: Implemented and committed cpachecker_v0 and cpachecker_v1, but did not complete or commit the cpachecker_v3 BMC and k-induction implementation.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Delivered two requirement patch files. The harness collected only cpachecker_v0 and cpachecker_v1 patches, leaving the final v3 deliverable absent.
serial.verification: Verified v0 and v1 outputs locally before cancellation. The official evaluator later passed v0/v1 but failed all four v3 benchmark value checks.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The first round timed out before v3 work, and the retry failed with provider.rate_limit after reading the v3 requirement, so the v3 requirement remained incomplete.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized all three required stages and reported full 3/3 requirement coverage.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same task and later read the v3 requirement, but did not complete it.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Requirement understanding was similar; completion differed because parallel finished v3 while serial stopped before implementing v3 and the retry failed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel chose one main owner for all stages and explicitly declined subagents because of tight sequential dependencies.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also had one actor and no delegation, with Agent and AgentSwarm disabled in the control.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There was no productive parallel decomposition to compare; the winning run was a completed single-owner implementation, not a coordinated multi-agent plan.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel had no child briefs, inter-agent interface contracts, or handoffs; the main actor kept shared design context locally across the stages.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child briefs or handoffs either; the retry reread v3 but did not progress beyond early LLM requests.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No cross-agent context boundary explains the outcome; the serial shortfall was loss of execution after v1 and a provider failure on retry.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel implemented the value analysis, predicate analysis, BMC, and k-induction modules.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implemented value and predicate analysis and committed v1, but no v3 implementation or commit appears before cancellation and retry failure.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The material implementation delta is the parallel completion of bmc.py and k_induction.py versus the serial absence of the required v3 stage.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel finalized all three local stage results into commits and patch files before closure.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial finalized v0 and v1 but the active first-round turn was cancelled before v3, and the second-round v3 attempt failed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel completed the local result lifecycle for every required stage; serial had no v3 result to package or evaluate.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel integrated the dependent stages in one workspace and the harness collected three requirement patches plus an agent test file.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial integrated only two completed stages; the harness collected two requirement patches and no agent tests.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There was no shared-state race. The delivery difference is that parallel included the v3 patch and serial did not.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran targeted v3 checks and a full acceptance run showing 12/12 correct, then the official evaluator passed every listed testcase.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial locally showed v0/v1 passes, but official evaluation failed all four v3 value checks.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had end-to-end acceptance evidence for all stages; serial had only partial local verification and failed the missing v3 obligations officially.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel finished in one round without timeout and closed after all requirements were done.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial timed out in round one and the round-two continuation failed with a provider 429.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The outcome gap is explained by ordinary run completion and retry failure, not by parallel fan-out, waiting, child cancellation, or other coordination behavior.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The pair is an official parallel-only pass. Parallel succeeded because the single main actor completed all three CPAchecker stages, including v3 BMC and k-induction, and verified 12/12 benchmarks before closure. Serial failed because it completed and committed only v0 and v1, then the first round was cancelled before v3 work and the retry failed with provider.rate_limit after reading the v3 requirement. This is a process-completion difference rather than a parallel coordination advantage.
parallel_contributors: Single main actor kept ownership of the dependent v0, v1, and v3 implementations.
All three requirement patches were produced and final local acceptance reported 12/12 correct.
serial_contributors: Round one timed out or was cancelled before v3 was implemented.
Round two failed with provider.rate_limit after reading the v3 requirement.
Only two requirement patch files were collected for evaluation.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel added bmc.py and k_induction.py and v3 regression coverage.
Serial did not deliver the BMC/k-induction implementation required for cpachecker_v3.
evaluator_effects: The official result directly reflects missing v3 acceptance outputs in serial; no evaluator anomaly is evident.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative contributors, not an exclusive root cause
